industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence moved towards the tape. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): third-quarter beats were sold (Sandvik down 5%, Atlas Copco down 8%, Hiab down 12%), Danske Bank's C-J (25 October) says 'a lot is priced in' with the order strength coming from data centres the market no longer pays for, and the exception is the non-AI compounder (Hexagon, 13% organic growth); against it, offshore services and nuclear have multi-year visibility and electrical equipment is still the physical bottleneck. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, C prior. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment, Diversified groups, Distributors, Test and measurement and Engineered components at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Five live holdings (19.35 points of the book) sit here, judged in component 4. Counter-case for D: a tape that sells beats is a regime statement; for B: the order data remain the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack. To D on a second week of beats sold with relative strength falling to F.

sector.key: O.4. Electrical equipment, grid and automation
sector.why: Neutral, carried, with both sides stronger again. The demand: Jefferies' power analyst (28 October) raised the 2027 US data-centre build to about 27 gigawatts from the low twenties on satellite imaging, Fortum's 22-year nuclear agreement and rising Nordic power forwards say the grid is the constraint. The tape: ABB fell 6% on 40% order growth because the strength was data centres and the market 'is not willing at all to pay up for beats related to DC and AI' (Danske Bank, 25 October); Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, C prior, improved from last week's F reading. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): grid programmes are debt-funded with the ten-year above 5%. Two live holdings, Alfen (4.60%) and Arteche (3.28%), judged in component 4. Counter-case for D: the market's refusal to pay for data-centre orders is new since the summer and may last; for B: the binding constraint on the largest capital-spending theme is this sector's product. Moves to B if relative strength returns to B with the AI-infrastructure proxies recovering; to D on an F reading with hyperscaler capital spending guides cut.

geography.why: Neutral, carried. No source spoke to Spain this week (a source pack is present, 2026-W43, and it carried nothing country-specific here), relative strength is not graded by country, and Richard's view is G10 and Europe-wide with no country line. An absence is an absence; no tilt.

items.criterion: Relative price more than 25% below its 52W high, read at the month-end

bullets.text: Sell signal at the 30-Oct month-end: Arteche's relative price was 34.7% below its 12-May-2026 52W high, after 18.8% at 30-Sep.
The whole Arteche holding (all three tranches, 4.28% of capital) sells at the Tue 3-Nov session; Arteche is not under the one-off in/out link.
Ending the sell signal at 30-Nov needs a relative price 14.8% higher, about €35.14 at a flat market.

items.criterion: Sector RS below 50 with Stock RS below 70, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal: Arteche's Sector RS was 25, below 50, but Arteche's Stock RS was 76, above 70.
Arteche's Stock RS fell 19 points in October, 8 of them on 30-Oct; Sector RS fell from 70 at 30-Sep.
A Stock RS of 69 or less at the 30-Nov month-end gives a sell signal while Sector RS stays below 50.

items.criterion: A tranche 30% below its highest close since purchase, with Stock RS below 70

bullets.text: No sell signal: tranches 1 and 2's 30% level is €26.39 (30% below the €37.7 highest close, 30-Sep), 13.8% below the 30-Oct close; tranche 3's is €22.26 (30% below its €31.8 purchase close).
A fall to €26.39 would very probably also take Arteche's Stock RS (76) below 70, triggering tranches 1 and 2.

items.criterion: Industry RS below 30, read each Friday

bullets.text: No sell signal: Industry RS (Industrials and capital goods) was 46 at 30-Oct, 16 points above 30.
79 on 9-Oct, 46 on 23-Oct, 53 on 29-Oct, 46 on 30-Oct; its 12-month low is 40.

items.criterion: The 200D MA of relative price flat or falling over the month, read each Friday

bullets.text: No sell signal: Arteche's relative 200D MA rose 3.03% over the month to 30-Oct.
At a flat relative price the relative 200D MA keeps rising until about early February 2027; the Fri 6-Nov reading is not at risk.

items.criterion: SS Sales or SS PT Net Upgrade Breadth below zero AND Stock RS below 50, read at the month-end

bullets.text: No sell signal: revenue and PT Net Upgrade Breadth were +33% each at 30-Oct (data file, 100-day count), and Stock RS 76.
The 2-Nov rebuild of the data file read the breadth counts; the earlier build had no analyst data for this test.

adds.criterion: The rules: no sell signal from the six Sell Criteria

bullets.text: The rules block an add: relative price more than 25% below its 52W high gave a sell signal at the 30-Oct month-end.
Arteche's relative price back inside the line at a month-end, about €35.14 at a flat market on 30-Nov.

adds.criterion: The rules: room below the holding's limit

bullets.text: Arteche is 4.28% of capital against the 6.68% limit for a Middle Innings Core Investment: 2.40% of room.
The limit governs purchases only and never forces a sale; the sell signal, not the limit, blocks an add.

adds.criterion: Where Arteche stands for an add: pulling back or basing; may be retesting or forming a VCP; healthily retesting or breaking out

bullets.text: Pulling back or basing: Arteche closed 0.8% below its rising absolute 200D MA on 30-Oct, below its 50D, 100D and 150D MAs.
The Master Dashboard reads "may be retesting" (healthy retest 4 of 6 tests); the retest has not held on closes and the 50D MA is below the 150D.
A close above the 50D MA (€32.32) on 1.5x volume would make it a healthy retest of a rising MA.

adds.criterion: Your add trigger: a positive retest of a rising MA

bullets.text: Partly present: Arteche pulled back to its rising absolute 200D MA, closing at most 1.7% below it on 4 of 7 sessions.
The bounce (27 to 29-Oct) came on 0.53x to 0.75x volume and failed on 30-Oct at the day's low.
A heavy-volume close back above €30.85 that holds; a close below €30.1 would end it.

adds.criterion: Your add trigger: a broadening of the case (momentum rising in guidance, sell-side estimates, technicals or peers)

bullets.text: Absent: no guidance since 28-Jul and Arteche's estimates flat since 30-Sep; the memo expects cuts, not raises.
Technicals are falling (Stock RS 95 to 76 in October); peers are mixed, with leaders' estimates rising and the cohort's falling.
The Strategic Plan 2030 above consensus, or Arteche leading a sector up day on heavy volume.
On 28-Oct you wrote that Arteche "has successfully retested the rising 200D MA today", with no view on adding; tranche 3 (1.00%) was bought on 29-Oct.
The same note names "whether to adhere to the rule triggered by a 25% fall from its relative high" as "the big decision-making issue".
